question: What is the V-shaped groove that divides the tongue into oral and pharyngeal parts?
explanation: The sulcus terminalis is a distinct V-shaped groove on the dorsal surface that anatomically separates the anterior two-thirds of the tongue from the posterior one-third. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h1)

question: A short lingual frenulum restricts movement in which condition commonly assessed in newborns?
explanation: Ankyloglossia, also known as tongue-tie, occurs when a short or tight lingual frenulum limits the range of motion of the tongue tip. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which muscle group is responsible for altering the actual shape of the tongue?
explanation: Intrinsic muscles originate and insert inside the tongue, allowing it to change its shape during speech and swallowing. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h2)

question: The main extrinsic muscle responsible for protruding the tongue forward is the:
explanation: Contraction of the genioglossus muscle pulls the tongue forward and out of the oral cavity. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which type of lingual papillae contains NO taste buds?
explanation: Filiform papillae provide mechanical grip and touch sensation but lack taste buds entirely. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h3)

question: Large, dome-shaped papillae arranged in a V-shaped line near the back of the tongue are:
explanation: Circumvallate papillae are large structures positioned in a V-shaped row immediately anterior to the sulcus terminalis. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve provides motor innervation to almost all muscles of the tongue?
explanation: Cranial nerve XII (hypoglossal) controls the motor movements of nearly all tongue muscles, with the lone exception of the palatoglossus. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h4)

question: Taste sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue is carried by which nerve?

options.A: Chorda tympani branch of facial nerve

explanation: The chorda tympani branch of cranial nerve VII transmits gustatory signals from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h4)

question: The primary arterial blood supply to the tongue comes from which main vessel?
explanation: The lingual artery branches off the external carotid artery to supply the entire muscular mass of the tongue. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h5)

question: Lymph fluid from the very tip of the tongue drains first into which lymph nodes?
explanation: The submental lymph nodes receive primary lymphatic drainage from the apex or tip of the tongue. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h5)

question: During the act of swallowing, the tongue primarily pushes the food bolus in which direction?

options.B: Upward and backward against the palate
options.D: Downward toward the floor of the mouth

explanation: The tongue creates a wave of pressure that pushes the food bolus upward and backward into the pharynx during deglutition. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h6)

question: Which process during eating relies most heavily on the mechanical manipulation of the tongue?
explanation: Mastication involves the tongue actively moving food between teeth to break it down safely and effectively before swallowing. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T4#GNS211_U4_T4_h6)
